Seminar Title:

Understanding of Cloudburst Events Using the Indian Ocean-Land- Atmosphere Coupled Modeling Framework

Seminar Type:

Krishna Kishore Osuri

Abstract:

In the context of global warming, the frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall have significantly increased. Such events often trigger floods and landslides, causing severe damage to human life, infrastructure, and socio-economic assets. As defined by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a cloudburst is high-intensity rainfall exceeding 100 mm/hr at a station or over a 20-30 sq km area. This study analyzes the cloudburst events using the long-term composite study and the latest Indian Ocean Land Atmosphere (IOLA) coupled model. The composite study revealed that cloudburst events commonly occur in the Himalayan regions and during the monsoon season, particularly in July and August. Analysis using the ERA5 reanalysis dataset for 44 cloudburst cases highlights stronger monsoonal flow, with moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal converging over the Himalayan region and orographically lifted, leading to heavy rainfall events such as cloudbursts. The IOLA model experiments are performed in two modes, with and without ocean coupling. The results show that the IOLA model well simulates cloudburst events with minimal spatial and temporal errors. The ocean-coupled simulation of the IOLA model yields better results than the uncoupled simulation, improving rainfall prediction skills. The skill score tests also indicate that the IOLA model consistently simulates well, with better scores (&gt0.4 for lower thresholds &lt10 mm and &gt0.2 for higher thresholds &gt10 mm). The Skill score tests also show that, after coupling the IOLA model, rainfall prediction skills improve by ~10-15%. Overall, the coupled IOLA model simulation can help to improve predictions of heavy rainfall events and cloudbursts. This study provides valuable insights for the modeling community, enhancing understanding of cloudburst dynamics through an advanced coupled Ocean&ndashLand&ndashAtmosphere modeling framework.

Keywords: Cloudburst, Numerical weather prediction, IOLA, Ocean coupling
